Plan: (1) build the raw intake record, (2) run a rule-based canonicalizer against the loss description, (3) assemble the parties / jurisdiction matrices and validation flags, (4) list what's still missing.

```python
import pandas as pd, re, json
from datetime import date

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 90)

INTAKE_DATE = date(2026, 10, 12)   # today, per system date

# ---------------- 1. RAW INTAKE (as reported) ----------------
raw = {
    "claim_ref":          None,                     # NOT SUPPLIED
    "policy_number":      "CP-2024-1187",
    "named_insured":      "Harborview Retail LLC",
    "claimant":           "Harborview Retail LLC",
    "claimant_role":      "Named insured / policyholder",
    "policy_eff":         "2024-01-01",
    "policy_exp":         "2024-12-31",
    "loss_location":      "4820 Meridian Ave N, Seattle, WA 98103",
    "date_of_loss":       "2024-11-15",
    "date_reported":      None,                     # NOT SUPPLIED
    "reported_by":        None,                     # NOT SUPPLIED
    "loss_description":   "pipe burst in the store's back room",
    "jurisdiction_state": "WA",
}

# ---------------- 2. CANONICALIZER ----------------
CANON_RULES = [
    (r"(burst|broken|ruptured|split)\s*(water\s*)?pipe|pipe\s*(burst|rupture|failure|break)",
     ("Water Damage", "Escape of water - plumbing system failure", "WTR-PLUMB-BURST", 0.95)),
    (r"sewer|drain\s*back[- ]?up|backup of sewer",
     ("Water Damage", "Backup of sewer or drain", "WTR-SEWER-BU", 0.90)),
    (r"sprinkler",
     ("Water Damage", "Sprinkler leakage / discharge", "WTR-SPRINKLER", 0.85)),
    (r"flood|storm\s*surge|overflow of (a )?(body of water|river)",
     ("Flood", "Flood / surface water (commonly excluded)", "FLOOD", 0.90)),
]

def canonicalize(text: str):
    t = text.lower()
    for pat, (cat, sub, code, conf) in CANON_RULES:
        if re.search(pat, t):
            return cat, sub, code, conf
    return "Unclassified", "Requires adjuster review", "UNK", 0.00

cat, sub, code, conf = canonicalize(raw["loss_description"])

# "back room" -> normalized premises descriptor
PREM_NORMALIZE = {"back room": "back room (stockroom / non-public area)"}
prem = raw["loss_description"]
for k, v in PREM_NORMALIZE.items():
    prem = prem.replace(k, v)

canonical_narrative = (
    f"On {raw['date_of_loss']}, a plumbing pipe ruptured in the {prem.split('the ')[-1]} "
    f"of the insured retail premises at {raw['loss_location']}, causing an escape of water "
    f"and resulting damage to [building interior / business personal property / stock - TO BE CONFIRMED] "
    f"at the described premises. Reported cause: plumbing system failure "
    f"(non-flood, non-sewer-backup)."
)

# ---------------- 3. BIND + VALIDATION ----------------
dol = pd.Timestamp(raw["date_of_loss"]).date()
eff = pd.Timestamp(raw["policy_eff"]).date()
exp = pd.Timestamp(raw["policy_exp"]).date()

bind = {
    "policy_bound_to_claim": True,
    "within_policy_period":  eff <= dol <= exp,
    "days_into_term_at_dol": (dol - eff).days,
    "days_remaining_at_dol": (exp - dol).days,
    "days_dol_to_intake":    (INTAKE_DATE - dol).days,
}

record = pd.DataFrame({
    "Field": list(raw.keys()),
    "Value": ["<MISSING>" if v is None else str(v) for v in raw.values()],
    "Source": ["Reported by user"] * len(raw),
})

canon = pd.DataFrame([{
    "Standardized loss category (L1)": cat,
    "Standardized loss type (L2)":      sub,
    "Internal cause code":              code,
    "Match confidence":                 conf,
    "Reported language (verbatim)":     raw["loss_description"],
    "Canonical loss description":       canonical_narrative,
}]).T.rename(columns={0: "Value"})

bind_df = pd.DataFrame({"Item": list(bind.keys()),
                        "Value": [str(v) for v in bind.values()]})

print("="*115); print("CLAIM INTAKE RECORD - RAW"+" "*60); print("="*115)
print(record.to_string(index=False))
print("\n"+"="*115); print("CANONICALIZED LOSS DESCRIPTION"+" "*60); print("="*115)
print(canon.to_string())
print("\n"+"="*115); print("POLICY BIND / PERIOD VALIDATION"+" "*60); print("="*115)
print(bind_df.to_string(index=False))
```

```python
# ---------------- 4. PARTIES & JURISDICTION ----------------
parties = pd.DataFrame([
    ["Harborview Retail LLC", "Named insured / claimant", "Policyholder (owns or leases 4820 Meridian Ave N)", "Stated by user", "Confirmed"],
    ["Harborview Retail LLC (rep.)", "Authorized representative / on-site contact", "TBD", "Not supplied", "MISSING"],
    ["?", "Producer / broker of record", "TBD", "Not supplied", "MISSING"],
    ["?", "Adjuster / examiner", "TBD", "Not supplied", "MISSING"],
    ["?", "Mortgagee / loss payee / lender", "Check declarations + loss payee clause", "Not supplied", "MISSING"],
    ["?", "Additional insureds", "Check declarations", "Not supplied", "MISSING"],
    ["?", "Landlord / property owner", "Critical if insured is a tenant (waiver of subrogation)", "Not supplied", "MISSING"],
    ["?", "Plumber / contractor / prior repair vendor", "Potential subrogation target (cause & origin)", "Not supplied", "MISSING"],
    ["?", "Restoration / mitigation vendor", "Emergency services performed; salvage & invoice evidence", "Not supplied", "MISSING"],
], columns=["Party", "Role", "Relevance", "Source", "Status"])

jurisdiction = pd.DataFrame([
    ["Loss location (situs)", "Seattle, King County, Washington", "User", "Confirmed"],
    ["Policy issuance / negotiation state", "Not stated (assumed WA)", "Not supplied", "VERIFY"],
    ["Governing law / venue", "To be read from policy: 'Governing Law' & suit-limitation clause", "Policy not in hand", "VERIFY"],
    ["Regulator", "Washington Office of the Insurance Commissioner (OIC)", "Standard", "Confirmed"],
    ["Claims-practice rules", "WAC 284-30-330 et seq. (Unfair Claims Settlement Practices); 10 working days to acknowledge (WAC 284-30-360); 15 working days to accept/deny after proof of loss (WAC 284-30-370)", "Standard", "CITE - confirm current text"],
    ["Bad-faith exposure", "RCW 48.30.015 (Insurance Fair Conduct Act) - treble damages available", "Standard", "CITE"],
    ["Contract suit limitation", "WA written-contract SOL = 6 yrs (RCW 4.16.040), but policy may contain a shorter suit-limitation clause; enforceability requires counsel review", "To be read from policy", "VERIFY"],
    ["Licensing", "Confirm adjuster licensing/registration under WA producer rules (RCW 48.17)", "Standard", "VERIFY"],
], columns=["Item", "Determination", "Basis", "Status"])

missing = pd.DataFrame([
    ["Identify", "Claim/loss reference number", "Required to open the claim file"],
    ["Identify", "Date reported / date of notice to carrier", "Drives late-notice & regulatory clock"],
    ["Identify", "Date of loss discovered (may differ from 2024-11-15)", "Continuous vs. sudden loss analysis"],
    ["Coverage", "Declarations page: limits, deductibles, coinsurance, valuation (RCV/ACV)", "Cannot quantify exposure"],
    ["Coverage", "Policy form & edition; is 4820 Meridian Ave N a *scheduled* location?", "Unscheduled premises = possible gap"],
    ["Coverage", "Water-related endorsements/exclusions (water damage, sewer & drain backup, mold/fungus, freeze)", "Determines whether peril is covered"],
    ["Coverage", "Business income / extra expense limit & 72-hr waiting period", "Business interruption exposure"],
    ["Loss", "Extent & scope: building interior, stock, fixtures, equipment; repair/replacement estimate", "Reserves"],
    ["Loss", "Mitigation performed, water extraction, drying, mold remediation", "Mitigation costs are typically recoverable"],
    ["Loss", "Cause & origin evidence: photos, plumber's report, pipe material/age", "Subrogation + coverage analysis"],
    ["Parties", "Mortgagee/loss payee, broker of record, adjuster assignment", "Payment & notice obligations"],
    ["Parties", "Is insured the owner or a tenant? Lease terms, waiver of subrogation", "Recovery & rights"],
    ["Jurisdiction", "Policy issuance state & governing-law provision", "Choice of law"],
], columns=["Category", "Missing item", "Why it matters"])

print("="*115); print("RELEVANT PARTIES"+" "*72); print("="*115)
print(parties.to_string(index=False))
print("\n"+"="*115); print("JURISDICTION"+" "*60); print("="*115)
print(jurisdiction.to_string(index=False))
print("\n"+"="*115); print("OPEN / MISSING INFORMATION"+" "*60); print("="*115)
print(missing.to_string(index=False))

record.to_csv("claim_intake_CP-2024-1187.csv", index=False)
print("\n[Saved] claim_intake_CP-2024-1187.csv")
```

**Intake recorded and canonicalized.**

**1. Claim bound to policy.** Policy `CP-2024-1187`, term 2024-01-01 → 2024-12-31. Date of loss 2024-11-15 falls **inside the term** (319 days into a 365-day term, 46 days remaining). Loss is therefore an occurrence within the policy period — assuming the loss premises at 4820 Meridian Ave N is a *scheduled* location, which I still need to verify.

**2. Canonical loss description.**
- Category (L1): **Water Damage**
- Type (L2): **Escape of water — plumbing system failure**
- Internal cause code: `WTR-PLUMB-BURST` (match confidence 0.95)
- Canonical narrative: *"On 2024-11-15, a plumbing pipe ruptured in the back room (stockroom/non-public area) of the insured retail premises at 4820 Meridian Ave N, Seattle, WA 98103, causing an escape of water and resulting damage to [building interior / business personal property / stock — TO BE CONFIRMED] at the described premises. Reported cause: plumbing system failure (non-flood, non-sewer-backup)."*

Two coding notes for the file: this peril is **not** flood/surface water and is **not** sewer-and-drain backup, so the flood exclusion and the separate backup-of-sewer-and-drain endorsement should both be inapplicable — but confirm. Also flag the **freeze/14-day** provisions in the form: a mid-November burst in Seattle isn't a freezing loss on its face, but if the pipe failed due to lack of heat, that clause could bite. Cause & origin evidence will resolve it.

**3. Parties identified.** Only two are confirmed: **Harborview Retail LLC** as named insured, and the same entity as **claimant** (policyholder). Every other role on the matrix — representative, broker of record, adjuster, mortgagee/loss payee, additional insureds, landlord, plumber/contractor, restoration vendor — is currently blank. The landlord and plumber rows matter most: the first because a tenant's lease often carries a waiver of subrogation, the second because a burst pipe is a classic subrogation candidate.

**4. Jurisdiction.** Loss situs = Seattle, King County, **Washington**. Regulator is the **WA Office of the Insurance Commissioner**; claims handling is governed by **WAC 284-30-330 et seq.** (10 working days to acknowledge, 15 working days to accept/deny after proof of loss), with bad-faith exposure under **RCW 48.30.015 (IFCA)**. Policy issuance state and the governing-law/venue provision are unconfirmed.

**5. One flag worth your attention now.** Intake date is 2026-10-12; date of loss is 2024-11-15 — roughly **696 days** of lag. If the policy contains a 12-month suit-limitation clause, that is a material issue and the notice date needs to be established immediately.

**To proceed, please supply:** claim reference number, **date reported to the carrier**, the **declarations page** (limits, deductible, valuation, scheduled locations), the **policy form and water-related endorsements**, and the **loss/scope estimate with mitigation invoices**. Also confirm whether Harborview owns or leases 4820 Meridian Ave N.
